root_idea.summary: The root centers on certainty: the removal of doubt and the establishment of a firm, settled judgment.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development ranges from knowing or becoming certain, through firm conviction, to the Quranic distinctions between certainty as knowledge, direct seeing, and realized truth in عِلْمُ الْيَقِينِ, عَيْنُ الْيَقِينِ, and حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ.

senses.definition: To be certain of something; to hold it as firmly known or true.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrences, the verb describes firm conviction or belief with certainty, generally without an expressed object.

senses.definition: To become certain; to become convinced after attaining firm knowledge.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction presents certainty as reached or established by the subject; it may take the matter or signs of which one becomes convinced as its object.

senses.definition: One who has become certain; one who is convinced.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of اِسْتَيْقَنَ, describing a person in a state of attained or established conviction.

senses.definition: One who is certain; one who holds something as firmly true.
senses.usage_conditions: Active participle of أَيْقَنَ; in the Quranic occurrences it describes people characterized by firm certainty or conviction.

senses.definition: Certainty: knowledge or conviction in which doubt has been removed and the judgment is firmly settled.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a noun for certainty and adjectivally for something certain or sure. It may qualify a proposition or an action; in وَمَا قَتَلُوهُ يَقِينًا, it marks the alleged killing as something not established with certainty. The expression عِلْمُ الْيَقِينِ denotes certainty at the level of knowledge.

senses.definition: Certainty attained through direct seeing or witnessing.
senses.usage_conditions: A construction-specific use in عَيْنُ الْيَقِينِ, contrasted with certainty known at the level of knowledge.

senses.definition: Certainty realized through direct encounter with the reality known.
senses.usage_conditions: A construction-specific use in حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ; the expression presents certainty as realized or experienced truth, rather than merely known or witnessed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To know something, become certain of it, or make sure of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form I verb may occur with a direct object or with بِـ; the knowing is described as either intuitive or inferential.
An adjectival use of يَقِينٌ distinct from its noun sense of certainty.

cautions: The distinctions among عِلْمُ الْيَقِينِ, عَيْنُ الْيَقِينِ, and حَقُّ الْيَقِينِ are construction-specific developments of يَقِينٌ, not three unrestricted meanings in every occurrence.
